# Settings reference

Every key of `.github/ship.json`, the user file, presets, contexts and overrides. How layers combine is explained in [the configuration guide](configuration.md).

| Key | Type | Default | Environment variable | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ship.publish.mode` | `auto` \| `never` | `"auto"` | `SHIP_PUBLISH_MODE` | Whether ship pushes and opens the pull request after committing: "auto", or "never" (as --local; ship publish publishes later). |
| `ship.publish.update` | `rebase` \| `merge` \| `none` | `"rebase"` | `SHIP_PUBLISH_UPDATE` | How a branch behind its base is brought up to date before publishing: "rebase" replays it on the base (the push then uses a lease), "merge" merges the base into it (no rewrite, a normal push), "none" publishes it as it is. A checkpoint comes first; on a conflict ship cancels and publishes as it is. |
| `ship.publish.overlaps` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_PUBLISH_OVERLAPS` | Before pushing, and in ship status, warn about the open pull requests into the same base that change the same or adjacent lines as the branch: a likely conflict for whoever merges second. It never stops a publication. |
| `ship.git.remote` | string | `"origin"` | `SHIP_GIT_REMOTE` | Remote ship fetches from and pushes to, and whose GitHub repository it works with. In a fork, pull requests still open on the parent repository. |
| `ship.commits.gitmoji` | `auto` \| `first` \| `after-type` \| `none` | `"auto"` | `SHIP_COMMITS_GITMOJI` | Where the gitmoji goes: "auto" follows the repository's last 50 commits (ship-it's "first" when fewer than 5 are conventional), "first" (✨ feat: x), "after-type" (feat: ✨ x) or "none" (feat: x). |
| `ship.commits.subjectMaxLength` | integer ≥ 20 | `50` | `SHIP_COMMITS_SUBJECTMAXLENGTH` | Longest subject, in characters (after "type(scope): "; a tracker ticket at the end does not count). |
| `ship.commits.headerMaxLength` | integer ≥ 30 | `72` | `SHIP_COMMITS_HEADERMAXLENGTH` | Longest title, gitmoji included (✨ feat(scope): subject). The planner drops the scope of a longer one. |
| `ship.commits.bodyWidth` | integer ≥ 40 | `72` | `SHIP_COMMITS_BODYWIDTH` | Column at which commit bodies (the why) are wrapped. |
| `ship.commits.types` | object: type → `{emoji, branchPrefix, label, release}` or `false` | `{}` | `SHIP_COMMITS_TYPES` | Changes to the built-in commit types, by type: {"emoji", "branchPrefix", "label", "release"} changes a type or adds one (a new type needs an emoji and a branch prefix), false removes a built-in type. label is the kind/ label of its pull requests ("": none); release its version increment (major, minor, patch or none; a breaking change is always major). ship types lists the result. |
| `ship.commits.scopes` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_COMMITS_SCOPES` | Scopes a title may use; empty: any scope. The planner drops a scope that is not listed. |
| `ship.commits.scopeRequired` | boolean | `false` | `SHIP_COMMITS_SCOPEREQUIRED` | Refuse a title without a scope. |
| `ship.commits.scopeFrom` | `folders` \| `none` | `"folders"` | `SHIP_COMMITS_SCOPEFROM` | Where the planner takes the scope from: "folders", the deepest folder the changed files share, or "none" (you write it). |
| `ship.commits.signoff` | `auto` \| `always` \| `never` | `"auto"` | `SHIP_COMMITS_SIGNOFF` | Add a Signed-off-by trailer (DCO) with the committer's identity, as git commit -s does. "auto": when the repository asks for it, that is when most of its last 50 commits carry one, its CONTRIBUTING file mentions the DCO or Signed-off-by, or it configures the DCO app (.github/dco.yml). |
| `ship.commits.sign` | `auto` \| `always` \| `never` | `"auto"` | `SHIP_COMMITS_SIGN` | Sign commits: "auto" follows git's commit.gpgSign, "always" signs (git commit -S) and refuses to commit without a signing key (user.signingKey), "never" does not sign (--no-gpg-sign). Rebases and merges made before a publication follow it too. |
| `ship.branches.maxWords` | integer ≥ 1 | `4` | `SHIP_BRANCHES_MAXWORDS` | Words kept from the subject in a branch name (stop words such as "the" are dropped first). |
| `ship.branches.maxLength` | integer ≥ 8 | `32` | `SHIP_BRANCHES_MAXLENGTH` | Longest description part of a branch name, after the prefix and the issue number. |
| `ship.branches.issue` | `first` \| `none` | `"first"` | `SHIP_BRANCHES_ISSUE` | "first" starts the branch description with the issue number or tracker ticket (feat/42-add-login), "none" leaves it out. |
| `ship.pullRequest.draft` | `unattended` \| `always` \| `never` | `"unattended"` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_DRAFT` | When a new pull request is a draft: "unattended" when nobody reviewed the plan in a terminal (--yes), "always", or "never". Work in progress commits, ship publish --draft and AI agents always open a draft. |
| `ship.pullRequest.base` | string | `""` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_BASE` | Base branch of new pull requests, and the branch ship brings a branch up to date with; empty: the default branch of the repository on GitHub (of the parent repository, in a fork). Closing keywords only work on the default branch: on another base, the issue is linked with Refs. |
| `ship.pullRequest.labels` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_LABELS` | Add the kind and size labels the repository already has. |
| `ship.pullRequest.labelPrefixes.kind` | string | `"kind/"` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_LABELPREFIXES_KIND` | Prefix of the kind labels: kind/feature, kind/bug… The commit types name the kinds (ship.commits.types.<type>.label). |
| `ship.pullRequest.labelPrefixes.size` | string | `"size/"` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_LABELPREFIXES_SIZE` | Prefix of the size labels: size/XS… (ship.pullRequest.sizes). |
| `ship.pullRequest.sizes` | object: size name → changed lines (0: the largest) | `{"XS":10,"S":30,"M":100,"L":500,"XL":1000,"XXL":0}` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_SIZES` | Size labels, by name (after the size prefix), and the number of changed lines, generated files excluded, under which each applies; 0 marks the size of everything larger. The default is Kubernetes' scale. |
| `ship.pullRequest.maxLines` | integer ≥ 1 | `400` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_MAXLINES` | Changed lines (generated files excluded) above which the plan warns and suggests a split. Reviews lose effectiveness beyond about 400. |
| `ship.pullRequest.template` | string | `"auto"` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_TEMPLATE` | Pull request body: "auto" fills the repository's pull request template when it has one (as GitHub finds it on the default branch), "ship" always uses ship-it's format, or the path of a template in the repository (for a .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ directory). |
| `ship.pullRequest.sections.why` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_SECTIONS_WHY` | Write the why of the commits (their bodies) in ship's own pull request body. |
| `ship.pullRequest.sections.testing` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_SECTIONS_TESTING` | Write the Testing section (the checks that passed locally, the Tested: notes) in ship's own pull request body. |
| `ship.pullRequest.sections.issue` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_SECTIONS_ISSUE` | Link the issue (Closes #12) in ship's own pull request body. |
| `ship.pullRequest.sections.changes` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_SECTIONS_CHANGES` | Sum up the diff in the pull request body: the files added, changed, renamed and removed, and the declarations added and removed. |
| `ship.pullRequest.reviewers` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_REVIEWERS` | Logins whose review is requested on a new pull request (never its author). A request GitHub refuses is a warning. |
| `ship.pullRequest.teamReviewers` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_TEAMREVIEWERS` | Teams of the repository's organisation, by slug, whose review is requested on a new pull request. A request GitHub refuses is a warning. |
| `ship.pullRequest.assignSelf` | boolean | `false` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_ASSIGNSELF` | Assign a new pull request to its author. |
| `ship.pullRequest.milestone` | `issue` \| `none` | `"issue"` | `SHIP_PULLREQUEST_MILESTONE` | "issue" puts a new pull request in the milestone of the issue it closes, "none" leaves milestones alone. |
| `ship.issues.keyword` | `Closes` \| `Fixes` \| `Resolves` \| `Refs` | `"Closes"` | `SHIP_ISSUES_KEYWORD` | Keyword linking the issue in the pull request body. |
| `ship.issues.trackerKeys` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_ISSUES_TRACKERKEYS` | Project keys of an external tracker (Jira, Linear), such as ACME: a ticket ACME-123 in the branch name ends the commit and pull request titles, "(ACME-123)", and the branch keeps it in upper case. |
| `ship.secrets.ignorePaths` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_SECRETS_IGNOREPATHS` | Glob patterns of files never scanned for secrets (false positives); dir/** for a whole directory. |
| `ship.secrets.rules` | list of `{id, pattern, keywords}` | `[]` | `SHIP_SECRETS_RULES` | Extra rules: an id, a Go regular expression (RE2) and the literal keywords a line must contain for the pattern to run (compared without case when the pattern has (?i)). The value reported is the first capture group, else the whole match. |
| `ship.secrets.disabledRules` | list of `private_key` \| `github_token` \| `aws_key` \| `anthropic_key` \| `openai_key` \| `groq_key` \| `google_key` \| `stripe_key` \| `slack_token` \| `npm_token` \| `url_with_password` \| `secret_assignment` \| `sensitive_file` | `[]` | `SHIP_SECRETS_DISABLEDRULES` | Built-in rules turned off, by id. |
| `ship.secrets.allow` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_SECRETS_ALLOW` | Findings accepted, by the fingerprint ship prints with each one (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 of the value, salted with the rule id), never by value: a value in a file would leak it. |
| `ship.gates.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_GATES_ENABLED` | Run the project's own checks for each ecosystem it uses (the package.json scripts lint, typecheck and test; gofmt, go vet and go test; cargo fmt, clippy and test; and so on for Python, PHP, Ruby, JVM and .NET) before every push. ship check gates runs them on demand, and beforeCommit before the commit too. false: no check runs. |
| `ship.gates.allowSkip` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_GATES_ALLOWSKIP` | Accept --skip-gates (troubleshooting). false: the checks always run before a push. |
| `ship.gates.beforeCommit` | boolean | `false` | `SHIP_GATES_BEFORECOMMIT` | Also run the checks before the commit of ship and ship_deliver: a red check refuses the commit. Off by default, so that a commit stays instant and the checks run once, before the push. |
| `ship.tidy.auto` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_TIDY_AUTO` | Run ship tidy at the start of ship: leave a branch whose pull request was merged for the updated base, with the work in progress. ship tidy itself always runs. |
| `ship.tidy.deleteMerged` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_TIDY_DELETEMERGED` | Delete the local branches whose pull request was merged and that hold nothing more (ship undo recreates them). |
| `ship.logs.keepRuns` | integer ≥ 1 | `20` | `SHIP_LOGS_KEEPRUNS` | Number of past runs whose journal is kept in each log directory (.git/ship/logs, or the user log directory). |
| `ship.logs.maxBytes` | integer ≥ 1048576 | `10485760` | `SHIP_LOGS_MAXBYTES` | Total size in bytes kept in each log directory; the oldest runs go first. At least 1 MiB. |
| `ship.logs.blackBoxBytes` | integer ≥ 65536 | `1048576` | `SHIP_LOGS_BLACKBOXBYTES` | Size in bytes of the in-memory black box (DEBUG records of the run), written to disk only when a run fails. At least 64 KiB. |
| `ship.stack.rebase` | `local` \| `github` | `"github"` | `SHIP_STACK_REBASE` | Who rebases the layers above a merged one: "github" (GitHub's own rebase, which creates signed replacement commits; ship stack sync only follows it) or "local" (ship stack sync rebases on this machine with your signing key, then pushes with a lease). A classic chain of pull requests is always rebased locally. |
| `ship.stack.maxLayers` | integer ≥ 2 | `5` | `SHIP_STACK_MAXLAYERS` | Most layers ship stack splits the work into; the smaller areas are grouped in the top layer beyond it. |
| `github.managedBy` | string | `""` | `SHIP_GITHUB_MANAGEDBY` | Tool already managing this repository (opentofu, terraform…): ship sync then only reports differences. |
| `github.labels.taxonomy` | `ship-it` \| `none` | `"ship-it"` | `SHIP_GITHUB_LABELS_TAXONOMY` | Label set to maintain. |
| `github.labels.areas` | list of strings | `[]` | `SHIP_GITHUB_LABELS_AREAS` | Names of area/ labels, usually the commit scopes. |
| `github.project.url` | string | `""` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_URL` | GitHub Project (v2) to keep up to date: its URL (https://github.com/orgs/acme/projects/7, https://github.com/users/ada/projects/3) or owner/number (acme/7). Empty: no project. The token needs the project scope (gh auth refresh -s project). |
| `github.project.statusField` | string | `"Status"` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_STATUSFIELD` | Single-select field holding the status. Empty: the status is left alone. |
| `github.project.todo` | string | `"Todo"` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_TODO` | Status of an open roadmap issue that has none yet (a status set by hand is kept). |
| `github.project.inProgress` | string | `"In progress"` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_INPROGRESS` | Status ship publish sets when it opens a pull request that closes an issue of the project. |
| `github.project.done` | string | `"Done"` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_DONE` | Status of a closed roadmap issue. |
| `github.project.dateField` | string | `""` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_DATEFIELD` | Date field that receives the milestone's due date, such as "Target date" (for the Roadmap view). Empty: off. |
| `github.project.phaseField` | string | `""` | `SHIP_GITHUB_PROJECT_PHASEFIELD` | Single-select field that receives the milestone's title, such as "Phase"; its options must exist (the REST API cannot add them). Empty: off. |
| `ui.language` | `auto` \| `en` \| `fr` | `"auto"` | `SHIP_UI_LANGUAGE` | Language of messages: "auto" reads SHIP_LANG, then the locale (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG). SHIP_LANG, when set, wins over this setting. |
| `ui.reviewScreen` | boolean | `true` | `SHIP_UI_REVIEWSCREEN` | Show the review screen of ship in a terminal; false asks one confirmation instead (the plan is printed first). |
| `ui.accessible` | boolean | `false` | `SHIP_UI_ACCESSIBLE` | Plain interface for screen readers: no full-screen review, one question per line, as --plain and SHIP_ACCESSIBLE=1. |
| `ui.color` | `auto` \| `always` \| `never` | `"auto"` | `SHIP_UI_COLOR` | Colours of the review screen: "auto" follows the terminal, "always" keeps them when the terminal is not detected as colour-capable, "never" removes them. NO_COLOR, when set, always wins. |
